routes.name: Red-White-Red Card, Very Highly Qualified Worker
routes.summary: Points-based card for top talent with a job offer in Austria. You need at least 70 points out of 100. Tied to the named employer for 24 months.

other: At least 70 points (qualifications, experience, language, age, Austrian studies)
Proof of housing, health insurance and enough money to live on

stay.note: Tied to the employer named in the application.

routes.name: Job-Seeker Visa for Very Highly Qualified Workers
routes.summary: Six-month visa to look for a job in Austria if you score at least 70 points but have no offer yet.

other: At least 70 points
Proof of housing, health insurance and enough money to live on

routes.name: Red-White-Red Card, Skilled Worker in a Shortage Occupation
routes.summary: For people trained in an occupation on Austria's shortage list, with a binding job offer. You need at least 55 points out of 90.

other: Completed training in a shortage occupation
At least 55 points
Employer must pay at least the legal or collective agreement minimum wage

routes.name: Red-White-Red Card, Other Key Worker
routes.summary: For other qualified workers with a job offer. Employer must pay at least 3,465 EUR gross a month (2026), pass a labor market test, and you need 55 points.

other: At least 55 points
Employer pays at least 3,465 EUR gross per month (2026 figure)
No equally qualified jobseeker registered with the AMS can fill the job

routes.name: Red-White-Red Card, Graduate of an Austrian University
routes.summary: For people with a degree from an Austrian university who find a job that fits their qualification. No points system. Student permits can be extended 12 months to job hunt.

eligibility.education: Degree from an Austrian university, college or private university (diploma, bachelor's, master's or doctorate)
other: Job offer must match your qualification and pay the usual minimum for junior graduates
Job offer must come within the 12-month job-search period

routes.name: Red-White-Red Card, Regular Worker in Tourism, Agriculture and Forestry
routes.summary: For seasonal workers who have already worked in Austria in the same industry and now have a permanent job offer. German A1 required.

other: Worked at least 7 months in the last 2 years as a registered seasonal worker in the same industry
Binding job offer for permanent employment
No labor market test

sources.label: Regular Workers in Tourism, Agriculture and Forestry

routes.name: Red-White-Red Card, Self-Employed Key Worker
routes.summary: For people starting a business that gives Austria a wider economic benefit, for example by bringing in at least 100,000 EUR, creating jobs or new tech. No points system.

investment.note: Example of ongoing investment capital transferred to Austria. Other benefits like jobs or know-how can also qualify.

other: Business must bring broader economic benefit to Austria
Business plan, proof of qualifications and health insurance needed

routes.name: Red-White-Red Card, Start-up Founder
routes.summary: For founders of an innovative company. You need 30,000 EUR in capital, at least 50% ownership and 50 points. Bonus points for 50,000 EUR more capital.

savings.note: Proven capital for the new company

other: At least 50 points
At least 50% equity share and personal control of management
Consistent business plan
10 bonus points for additional capital of at least 50,000 EUR

routes.name: EU Blue Card Austria
routes.summary: For university graduates with a job offer paying at least 55,678 EUR a year (2026). No points system. Needs a labor market test.

eligibility.education: Completed tertiary study of at least 3 years (ICT and service managers can use 3 years of comparable work experience instead)

routes.name: Red-White-Red Card plus
routes.summary: Follow-up card with unlimited access to the Austrian labor market. Also used for family members of card holders. Valid 1 year, or 3 years after 2 years of lawful stay and Integration Agreement Module 1.

other: Card or Blue Card holders: employed under the card conditions for 21 of the last 24 months
Family: spouses and partners must be 21+, children under 18
First-time family applicants need German A1, except family of Very Highly Qualified Workers, Blue Card or researchers

stay.note: 3 years if you have lived in Austria lawfully for 2 years and completed Module 1.

routes.name: Settlement Permit, Private Individual (quota, no gainful employment)
routes.summary: For people who want to live in Austria without working, like retirees or people with independent means. Limited yearly quota and German A1 for first applications.

income.note: Single person, 2026. Couples 4,128.24 EUR per month, plus 403.76 EUR per child.

eligibility.language: CEFR A1 German (first application, with exemptions)
other: Needs an open quota place
Health insurance and suitable housing required
The page does not clearly state the fee for this permit

stay.note: Generally 1 year. 3 years if Module 1 is done and you lived lawfully in Austria the last 2 years.

routes.name: Settlement Permit, Artist
routes.summary: For employed or self-employed artists. Needs proof of artistic training or past work and, if self-employed, a contract of more than six months.

other: Employer declaration if employed, or written contract of over 6 months if self-employed
Proof of artistic training or description of past works

routes.name: Settlement Permit, Researcher
routes.summary: For researchers with a hosting agreement with a research institution. Valid 2 years, with one 1-year extension to job hunt or start a company. No German A1 needed.

other: Hosting agreement with a research institution
Exempt from the German A1 requirement

routes.name: Temporary residence permits (ICT, seconded worker, self-employed, volunteer, social service, cross-border)
routes.summary: Short-term permits for stays tied to one purpose, such as intra-company transfers, posted workers, contract-based self-employment and volunteering. Details and fees are on separate official pages.

other: Income at or above 1,308.39 EUR per month for a single person (2026)
Health insurance and suitable housing, with some exceptions
Duration and fees not stated on the overview page, check with the Austrian consulate

routes.name: Residence Permit, Student
routes.summary: For university students enrolled in a course of at least 40 ECTS credits. After graduating you can renew once for 12 months to look for work or start a business.

income.note: Under 24. Over 24 it is 1,308.39 EUR per month.

other: Extensions need proof of study progress
Work up to 20 hours a week needs an employment permit
Fees and duration not stated on the page

routes.name: Family Reunification (spouse, registered partner, minor children)
routes.summary: Residence title for spouses, registered partners and unmarried children under 18 of people living in Austria. German A1 usually needed for the first application.

income.note: Single, 2026. Couples 2,064.12 EUR, plus 201.88 EUR per child.

other: Spouses and partners must be 21 or older, children under 18
No quota for family of Red-White-Red Card, Blue Card, Austrian citizens or researchers. Other family titles can be limited each year.

stay.note: 3 years after 2 years of lawful stay and Module 1.

routes.name: Long-term Resident EU (permanent residence)
routes.summary: Permanent residence status after 5 years of continuous lawful stay and Integration Agreement Module 2. Free access to the labor market.

other: 5 years of uninterrupted lawful residence
Integration Agreement Module 2 completed
Income, health insurance and housing requirements met

routes.name: Austrian Citizenship by Naturalization
routes.summary: Generally 10 years of legal continuous residence, at least 5 on a residence permit. You need German skills, a citizenship knowledge test and stable income. Apply at the provincial government office.

eligibility.language: German, usually shown with Integration Agreement Module 2
other: Stable own income for an average of 36 months in the last 6 years, no set amount on the page
Clean criminal record
Test on Austria's democracy, history and your province
Exceptions exist, for example for native German speakers

citizenship.note: Official pages list giving up your previous nationality as a general requirement. Exceptions were not confirmed, check with the provincial authority.

routes.name: Austrian Citizenship by Descent
routes.summary: Children of an Austrian mother get citizenship at birth. Same if the parents are married and the father is Austrian. If unmarried, the father must recognize the child within 8 weeks.

other: Mother Austrian: automatic
Married parents, father Austrian: automatic
Unmarried, father Austrian: father recognizes child or a court establishes parenthood within 8 weeks. Later recognition can use a simplified process.

citizenship.note: A child of parents with different nationalities can hold both if the other country also grants citizenship by descent. The child does not have to choose at adulthood under Austrian law.

routes.name: Short stay, visa-free or Schengen visa
routes.summary: Austria is in the Schengen area. Many nationalities can stay up to 90 days in 180 days without a visa. Others need a Schengen visa for stays up to 6 months. Stays over 6 months need a residence permit.

other: Check the official Schengen visa-free list for your passport
Exact fees and the full list not confirmed, the foreign ministry site blocked bots

routes.name: Asylum and international protection
routes.summary: Austria grants asylum and other protection under national and EU law. Start with the official migration site and the federal asylum office.

other: Process details not confirmed from an official page in this pass

routes.name: EU, EEA and Swiss free movement
routes.summary: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens and their family members get special residence rules in Austria. The official site lists a settlement permit for extended family members of EEA or Swiss nationals.

other: Details on registration and rights not confirmed from an official page in this pass
